summary: The Treasurer is the state's banker: she sells California's bonds, manages its cash investments, and sits on the CalPERS and CalSTRS pension boards. The seat is open: Fiona Ma is term-limited and running for Lieutenant Governor. Democrat Eleni Kounalakis, the two-term Lieutenant Governor who dropped a run for governor in August 2025, placed first in the June 2 primary with 36.69%; Republican Jennifer Hawks, a retired businesswoman, placed second with 24.00%.

positions.stance: As a UC Regent and CSU Trustee she has regularly voted against tuition increases. (CalMatters voter guide)
Cites her years running a Sacramento real estate development firm and her service as U.S. Ambassador to Hungary. (CalMatters; Wikipedia)
Wants taxpayers to be able to see where and how each dollar is spent. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)
Calls the state's bond investments reckless and says California should not take on more bond debt for unfinished projects. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)
Pledges to protect retirement security as a CalPERS and CalSTRS board member. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)

key_differences: Kounalakis is a two-term statewide officeholder; Hawks has never held elected office and presents that as independence.
Hawks's platform is about issuing less debt; Kounalakis has not campaigned on cutting bond issuance.
Neither candidate has published a detailed investment-policy plan that this research found.

sources.title: Ballotpedia: Jennifer Hawks (certified primary results, candidate survey)
